sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number for login and HR operations; email: unique lookup for authentication and contact; manager_id: frequent queries to retrieve direct reports for manager workflows; department: filtering and grouping employees by department; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees for leave eligibility checks
table leave_types | fields: id, code, name, description, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: code: unique lookup by leave type code for policy assignment and request filtering

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: lookups of policies by leave type for request validation; is_active: filtering active policies during leave request processing

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of leave requests by employee for self-service views; status: filtering requests by status (pending approvals, approved, rejected) for manager workflows; leave_type_id: filtering requests by leave type for reporting and balance calculations; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: lookups of requests approved by a specific manager

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of balances by employee for self-service dashboard; policy_id: lookups by policy for accrual batch processing; fiscal_year: filtering balances by fiscal year for annual reset and reporting; employee_id, fiscal_year: composite access pattern — an employee's balance for a given year is the most common query

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: lookups of audit trail for a specific entity (e.g. all changes to a leave request); performed_by: lookups of actions performed by a specific user for compliance; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports; action: filtering by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE, etc.)

data_notes: Persistence slice designed for the leave management module. Six conceptual tables: employees (self-referencing manager hierarchy), leave_types (enumeration of annual/sick/emergency/etc.), leave_policies (per-type entitlement rules), leave_requests (the core transactional entity with status lifecycle), leave_balances (per-employee-per-policy-per-fiscal-year tracking), and audit_logs (GP-002 compliance for all state-changing operations). Six repository interfaces, each backed by a concrete Pg*Repository using the existing pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts. Index rationale reflects access patterns: employee lookups, status filtering for manager approval queues, date-range overlap detection, fiscal-year balance queries, and audit trail retrieval by entity and performer.
